correctness.rationale: If two ordered hyperbola pairs have the same nonzero vector sum, then their first-coordinate sums agree and equality of inverse-coordinate sums forces the same product, so the unordered pair is determined; every nonzero pair-sum fiber therefore has size at most two. The zero fiber consists of all \(q-1\) ordered antipodal pairs. This gives the same exact weighted-energy identity as in the anisotropic case. Antipodal-pair optimization forces equal moduli within and across pairs and common phase of the products, yielding \(\mathcal Q\le3(q-2)S^2/(q-1)\) and hence the stated normalized constant. Independent brute-force reconstruction for \(q=3,5,7,11,13\) reproduced zero-fiber size \(q-1\), nonzero-fiber maximum two and energy \(3(q-1)(q-2)\); the actual verifier repeats these checks through prime 101 and certifies a nontrivial phase extremizer.

value.rationale: The multiplicative hyperbola is a canonical finite-field curve. Replacing the known uniform extension estimate by an exact norm and complete extremizer class is a natural sharp endpoint problem, with the split conic's \(q-1\) geometry producing a distinct constant from the anisotropic \(q+1\) case.

final_claim: For the finite-field multiplicative hyperbola \(H=\{(t,t^{-1}):t\in\mathbb F_q^\times\}\), \(q\) odd, with normalized surface measure and ambient counting measure, the exact sharp fourth-moment extension constant is \(R_H^*(2\to4)^4=3q^2(q-2)/(q-1)^3\); the nonzero extremizers are exactly constant-modulus functions whose antipodal products have one common argument.
limitations: Odd finite fields and the multiplicative hyperbola only.
